# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Focused verification

For an unchanged-contract repair, use `creative:repair:check`: prove the affected
runtime action first, then focused static checks. Run full verification once for
the stable candidate; reuse exact successful command/source receipts rather than
having implementer and verifier rerun the same suite. Runtime evidence and affected
independent review remain required. See the creative-triad skill for the narrow
repair route. Existing runs retain their archived instruction versions.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the
space-station chapter. Do not refuse or defer this work on the basis of an
older freeze — earlier revisions of this file carried one, and it expired.

What still applies:

- **Creative-Triad and registry gates are the remaining barrier** between a new
  chapter and the runtime. Route the work through them; do not route around.
- **Sequencing is owner-directed: do not rush to the station.** Making the
  existing story enjoyable comes first, and the need to leave must emerge from
  play rather than from a new content hook.
- **The demo's release surface is unchanged** — it still stops at
  `ch4-arrival`, and publishing remains a separate decision. Building past it
  is allowed; shipping it in the demo is not implied.
- **Shipped copy and audio remain protected baselines.** Changing a protected
  audio/runtime path is still a contracted change, not an incidental one.
- **"Anchorage" is retired as a name.** The location is the **space station**.

# Arrival COMMON probe preparation — bounded instrumentation only

**Roles prepared:** `arrival-common-manual`, `arrival-common-earned`
**Runtime executed:** NO. No browser, no GPU, no preview, no capture, no build, no `npm test`.
**Game / shared source / contract / signature mutated:** NO.
**Machine-readable report:** `arrival-common-probe-prep-report.json`
(sha256 `648d8ee31767b51c73ea152678441635fcec7c98ab8170de3d967709a28249f4`).

## What was created

| New (owned) | Copied byte-exactly from |
|---|---|
| `verifier/probes/arrival-common-manual/` | `verifier/probes/common-manual-focused/` |
| `verifier/probes/arrival-common-earned/` | `verifier/probes/earned-continue/` |
| `logs/arrival-common-probe-prep/` (9 logs) | — |

**Originals are byte-exact.** Every file under both original folders was sha256'd
before any work and again after all edits; the two lists are identical (`diff`
empty). The eight before/after hashes are listed in the JSON report.

## Dependencies are pinned, not read live

`cgContract.mjs`, `ownedSession.mjs` and `sourceSnapshot.mjs` were copied into
each new probe folder as `*.pinned.mjs` and are imported from there, so a
concurrent edit to `verifier/probes/lib/*` cannot change these lanes' meaning.
The copies sit at the **same directory depth** as the originals, so
`cgContract`'s `RUN_DIR = resolve(HERE,'..','..','..')` and `REPO_ROOT` /
`CAPTURES` resolve exactly as before; each probe folder is a sibling of its
original, so `../../../../../../main/tools/lib/evidence.mjs` is also unchanged.
`evidence.mjs` is deliberately **not** copied (it transitively imports sibling
main tooling whose relative paths a copy would break); its hash at preparation
time is recorded in each `pin.json` so drift is detectable. CPU tests assert the
pinned bytes against `pin.json`.

## 1. Earned Origin gate — tightened (`arrival-common-earned`)

Per `producer-earned-continue-prep-review.json` → `requiredBeforeRuntime` 1 and 2,
`earnedOriginGate` now additionally requires:

- `landedActivePlanetId === '-1,-1'` **exactly** (the signed Origin) — not merely
  "different from the departure body";
- `anc.cg.origin-landed` present in the **named** `signedSceneAv.activationHistoryAnchorIds`;
- `anc.cg.origin-landed` present in the **chapter** fired-anchor history; and
- that the chapter anchor history was actually **read** (a `null` read is refused
  as UNMEASURED, never passed).

Everything already required is preserved: the real latched `story:ch13-origin-landed`
milestone (nothing preseeded), `surface`/`fps` modes, `supported === true`, a
finite grounded pose, a measured live frame rate ≥ `minFps`, the non-empty named
history, the array-shape check, and the raw `Object.keys(av).length` retained as
explicitly labelled **non**-evidence. All raw traces (full named history, fired
anchors, anchor id/event/beat, activation sequence, counts, and the two per-side
booleans) are reported on refusal **and** on pass.

Discriminating CPU checks, all passing:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| different wrong planet `3,7` (not the departure body) | refused, names the signed-Origin rule |
| near-miss `-1,-1:p2` | refused |
| **non-empty** lift-only AV history `['anc.cg.origin-lift']` | refused, raw history preserved |
| chapter-only origin history (AV lacks it) | refused, both sides reported |
| AV-only origin history (chapter anchors lack it) | refused |
| chapter anchor history not read (`null`) | refused as UNMEASURED |
| **exact earned all-state** (`-1,-1` + anchor in BOTH histories + grounded + fps) | **passes** |
| tightened gate with an unavailable signed-AV bridge | still refused |

The Continue lane is untouched: actual save bytes via the shipped
`beforeunload → doSave → saveWorld` path, no deep reseed on the Continue boot
(`?story=` / `movie=1` still refused), a real new physical action with its own
signed anchor, the by-name no-replay proof, and all preflight / role / lock /
served-identity / manifest-rehash / non-empty-capture guards.

The inherited "why a copy exists" run-4/run-5 narrative is retained only as
clearly labelled inherited prose with the producer's qualification stated inline.
No new claim rests on it.

## 2. Passive entry observation (both lanes)

`entryObservation.mjs` (identical in both folders) records, passively:
`pointerlockchange` / `pointerlockerror`; page `console` warn/error and
`pageerror`; per-click `isTrusted`, `pointerType`, `pointerId`, `buttons`,
`detail`, `sourceCapabilities.firesTouchEvents`, `target` and `currentTarget`;
focus state (`hasFocus`, `visibilityState`, `activeElement`, `pointerLockElement`,
`navigator.userActivation`); touch state (`maxTouchPoints`, `ontouchstart`,
pointer coarse/fine, `hover:none`, mounted touch-control DOM); and policy state
(`__storyInputPolicy`, permissions-API presence).

`describeEventTarget` fixes exactly the defect
`entry-discriminator-report.json` recorded — both observers threw
`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')` on a
window/document `currentTarget` — and handles Window, Document, Element,
element-like objects with a non-string `tagName`, text nodes, other node types,
plain objects, functions, primitives, `null`, `undefined`, and objects whose
getters throw. `entryObserverSource()` embeds `describeEventTarget.toString()`,
so the page-side function is literally the CPU-tested source, and a test asserts
that embedding.

**Explicitly not done:** no `requestPointerLock`, no forced or synthetic click,
no `dispatchEvent`, no game-handler patch, no injected key state, no focus or
permission/policy edit, no `preventDefault`/`stopPropagation` (listeners are
passive), and **no new loop, retry or timeout** — the prior 16:31 cause is
UNKNOWN and nothing was tuned to it. The manual lane keeps its ordinary
shipped-canvas click path (unchanged, up to 3 real clicks) and its pointer-lock /
focus gate byte-unchanged; observation gates nothing. Console sinks are bounded
(max 400) with overflow **counted**, never silently dropped, and absent fields
are reported as UNMEASURED rather than guessed.

prerequisite gates, calibrated pulse/coast policy measured from the four live
holds, reference/deviation modes with the strict physical 18-unit COMMON route,
identity/lock/served-byte ownership, non-empty output refusal, before/after source
snapshots, and the owned-session cleanup guard.

`activeRole` is hardcoded as `arrival-common-manual` (passed to
`preflightDecision`; a different `activeRole` in `verifier-control.json` refuses
launch) and `arrival-common-earned` (default `--role`). Each lane expects its own

states a "99 file" manifest count — it re-hashes every path the **current**

binding/refusal fixture and the real inherited-flock kernel lock-ownership test.

Inherited → current check counts: manual ≈95 → 112, earned 69 → 108.

- Manual COMMON reference/deviation remain **NOT MEASURED**.
- The 16:31 entry failure cause remains **UNPROVED**; the new observation would
  record a *future* refusal's own native reason, and explains nothing about the past.

 *   preservation. earned-1/earned-2 tried ?story=ch13-return but their flights

 *   survey: story:ch13-origin-landed latched at 73 791 ms, beat ch13-survey,
 *   objective ch13:survey:start. That unblocks a PRIMARY earned entry.
 *
 *   PREPARATION ONLY. Nothing in this file has been executed against a browser.
 *   No result here is a capture, a verification or an acceptance.
 *
 * ARRIVAL LANE COPY (2026-09-06). Byte-copied from
 * verifier/probes/earned-continue/, which was NOT edited. Differences:
 * activeRole is `arrival-common-earned`; the shared verifier helpers are PINNED
 * into this folder; `--out` must be an ABSOLUTE capture directory; the earned
 * Origin gate is TIGHTENED (exact signed Origin `-1,-1` plus
 * anc.cg.origin-landed in BOTH the named signed-AV activation history AND the
 * chapter fired-anchor history); and a PASSIVE entry observation (console/
 * pageerror, pointerlockchange/error, click isTrusted/pointerType/
 * sourceCapabilities/target/currentTarget, focus/touch/policy state) is
 * recorded. Continue still proves itself from ACTUAL save bytes, with no deep
 * reseed, a real new action and an explicit no-replay check.
 *
 * HISTORY QUALIFICATION (producer-earned-continue-prep-review.json,
 * "qualifications"): the WHY-A-COPY-EXISTS narrative above is INHERITED prose
 * from the original probe and its run-4 / run-5 attribution was NOT accepted by
 * the producer (run-5 retained 1305 bytes and lawfully resumed at the departure
 * body because the FIXTURE lacked origin-landed; a separate later repair fixed a
 * bootstrap overwrite). Nothing in this lane's assertions depends on that
 * narrative, and no claim here re-states it as established.
 *
 * UNEXECUTED CLI EXAMPLE — placeholders only. This command has NOT been run and
 * MUST NOT be copied verbatim: the old 38007 port and the old dc63fba… manifest
 * are examples of the SHAPE, never defaults. The runtime owner substitutes the
 * CURRENT root-published URL, source-manifest sha and served index/bundle hashes
 * (re-hashed at release, not remembered from preparation).
 *
 *   flock -x <ABS_HEAVY_LOCK_PATH> -c '\
 *     node verifier/probes/arrival-common-earned/earned-continue-probe.mjs \
 *       --url <CURRENT_ROOT_PUBLISHED_URL> \
 *       --expect-source-manifest <CURRENT_SOURCE_MANIFEST_SHA256> \
 *       --heavy-lock <ABS_HEAVY_LOCK_PATH> --heavy-lock-fd <INHERITED_FD> \
 *       --role arrival-common-earned \
 *       --out <ABSOLUTE_FRESH_CAPTURE_DIR>'
 *
 *   CPU-only self-checks (no browser, no GPU):
 *     node verifier/probes/arrival-common-earned/selftest.mjs
 *     node verifier/probes/arrival-common-earned/earned-continue-probe.mjs --self-test
 *
 * ACTUAL PARTIAL WorldSave / Continue TEST — bounded to ONE question:
 *
 *   Does a REAL, physically earned, UNFINISHED ch13 survey drawing survive the
 *   shipped save -> Continue lifecycle, and can a NEW signed action then be
 *   performed and accepted on the restored state?
 *
 * WHAT THIS IS NOT
 * ----------------
 *   - not a chapter verification, not a movie journey, not a cold-run measure;
 *   - no teleport, no progress/milestone setter, no direct predicate call, no
 *     hand-constructed save payload, no relaxed arrival/route rule;
 *   - the movie rail is used ONLY as the shipped way of reaching the drawing
 *     state (exactly as capture world-final/survey-1 did). Where the rail
 *     stalls, ORDINARY shipped movement keys are pressed. Any such key input is
 *     labelled `scripted-input` and NEVER counted as zero-rescue movie success.
 *
 * LIFECYCLE UNDER TEST (all shipped code paths, one labelled entry fixture):
 *   0. PREFLIGHT WITH NO BROWSER: root role/readiness binding, an inherited
 *      exclusive heavy-lock receipt, the ACTUAL served index+bundle byte hashes,
 *      a dynamic re-hash of EVERY path the CURRENT
 *      root-published manifest lists (the count is whatever that manifest says
 *      at release; no historical file count is assumed here), and a non-empty
 *      capture refusal. Any refusal stops before Chromium is launched.
 *   1. `?story=ch13-return&journeyprobe=1&debug=1&movie=1` — the INITIAL
 *      deep-link prerequisite fixture (labelled). It seeds the ch13-return entry
 *      only; it does NOT seed story:ch13-origin-landed and NOTHING here preseeds
 *      an origin landing. The shipped movie-scripted physical flight must earn
 *      it, and the earned-origin gate refuses everything downstream otherwise:
 *      real activePlanetId handoff, surface/fps control, grounded support, a
 *      measured live frame rate, the latched milestone, and NAMED signed-AV
 *      anchor history (never an object-key count).
 *   2. Earn the partial recording with actual shipped movement/[F] inputs, and
 *      CATCH the capture at the partial checkpoint — before the movie rail can
 *      carry the survey through offer/route-test.
 *   3. Save through the shipped autosave-on-unload path (App.tsx `beforeunload`
 *      -> doSave(true) -> saveWorld -> serializeCommonGroundForWorld), fired by
 *      a same-tab navigation away from the game. The ACTUAL serialized
 *      localStorage bytes are copied out as evidence before the browser closes.
 *   4. Boot the menu with NO story deep link and press the real Continue button
 *      (LandingMenu -> beginStory -> storyEntryPoint). Browser storage is
 *      retained across the navigation; nothing is re-seeded.
 *   5. Compare restored route/identity/actor progress, check that no earned
 *      action replays into fresh AV history, then perform a NEW action (walk to
 *      E with ordinary keys, offer the span with [F]) and check its signed AV
 *      anchor is accepted.
 *
 * Everything is measured; nothing here decides acceptance.
 */
